body: **Round 5, item by item: in `4ed6449`,** one commit on `4a284f9`. `main` is still `561bd84`, and `git diff --name-status 561bd84..4ed6449` lists only this PR's own files. **1. High (regression): a key right after `%3d` or `%3a` wasn't read.** Fixed. - **A key may start right after any percent-escape:** `(?:(?--db-token=`, `state%3A…%22token%22%3dtoken:`, `%7B%22pw%22%3A…`, `%26pin%3D…`, `%26pw%3D…`, `%0A_auth%3D…`, `\n_auth=…`, `\npw=…` and `\tpsk=…`; - `x%3dadpw=1` and `unpw=1` are kept, since a word that only ends so is no escape; - runs of `\n` are still read in well under a second. - **Mutants:** without the percent alternative, without the strip, and without the hex or the letter strip: all killed. **2. High (regression): a `<` in an attribute hid a secret-named tag.** Fixed as you proposed: `/<(?:[\w.-]{1,64}:)?([\w.-]{1,128})(?=[\s/>])/g`. Attributes aren't scanned at all. - **Tests:** - ``, ``, ``, ``, `` and `` are masked; - `bold and it` is kept. - **The timing test's bound is 3 s now,** with 24 cells of 256 KB. They take well under a second alone. - **Mutants:** `[^<>]` put back, and `/` dropped from the lookahead: both killed. **3. Medium: the fold's first five names hid a seeded column.** Fixed with your first suggestion. - **Diff entries carry `fieldsBefore`:** the before snapshot's declared fields, already read by `diffSnapshots`, and shared, not copied. - **The flag lists seeded fields first:** in `column-dropped`, `fields` starts with the dropped fields the base pane's before snapshot declares too, then the PR's own, each group by name. `seeded` counts the first group. - **Test, your shape:** - The PR adds `aa_tmp_0000`–`aa_tmp_0004` to the seeded `users`, then drops them and `email`. - The one flag is red, with `count: 6`, `seeded: 1` and `fields: ['email', 'aa_tmp_0000', …]`. - With only its own columns dropped, `seeded` is 0. - **Mutants:** sorted names back, and `fieldsBefore` null: both killed. **Low, word-only names after an escape.** Fixed with 1. **Low, the pair rule took only the first name-like key.** Fixed. Any string-valued name-like key that looks secret names the pair. - **Tests:** `{key: 'mail.smtp', name: 'Password', value}`, `{k: 'row-17', name: 'password', value}` and `{key: 'setting_42', name: 'SMTP password', value, updated}` are masked. So are the 8-key `{key: 'password', value, …}` and `{Key: 'api_token', Value, …}` (the strict branches). - **Rows, from the residuals:** a row shaped as a pair has its value fields masked: a settings table's `{id, key: 'smtp_password', value}` and `{id, name: 'STRIPE_SECRET_KEY', value}`. A neutral row (`site_title`) keeps its value, and a cleared value still shows. **Low, DSN and attribute variants.** Widened, with a test each: - **DSNs:** - the password runs up to the last `@` (`root:p@ss…@tcp(…)`); - any network: `tcp6`, `unix`, `cloudsql` and the like; - and `@/`. - **The DSN nit:** the password class leaves out `:`, so a run stops at the next `:`. 256 KB of `a:` take well under a second, and the code comment no longer says "each linear". - **Attributes:** - `key`, `name`, `id`, `type` and `value` are matched in any case, with values quoted either way or not; - so ``, ``, a single-quoted value holding `"`, and `` are masked. - **Listed in the README** under "what masking misses": a DSN password with a `:` in it, and an element value holding `>`. **Low, a left-out `unverified` sorted after every other base-pane flag.** Fixed. A base-pane collection's `unverified` flag now stands with what loses rows when the PR's snapshots may have left it out, which can hide a drop or a wipe. That covers a PR diff entry with `omitted` set, and a collection the PR diff lacks. - **Test:** a wipe hidden by padding is flagged before another seeded collection's `column-dropped`. A cut-short collection's `unverified` still comes after a `mass-change`. - **The reply's claim was wrong,** as you said: at `4a284f9` it sorted after the column and mass-change flags. It doesn't now. **Low, the 25 mutants.** Tests added for those named: - **`column-dropped` shared by count:** the base drops `legacy` and the PR drops `email`, trusted. The flag is red, not shared. - **The 8-key strict pairs** (above). - **`cleared` on 3 rows where the base cleared 1:** `shared: false`, `pr 3`, `base 1`. - **`key-lost` before `column-dropped`,** and `delete` before `mass-change`. - **Attribute and PEM forms:** ``, ``, PKCS#8 `BEGIN PRIVATE KEY`, EC and OPENSSH keys. - **Other shapes:** - `mysqldump -p…`, `basic dXNlcjpwYXNz` (lower case), and `-password x`; - `%27password%27%3A…`, `root:pw@unix(…)`, and 31 spaces before `=`; - `X-OAUTH-BASIC`, and the `gho_`, `github_pat_`, `xoxb-` and `sk-` prefixes. **Low, other residuals.** - **Fixed:** - rows shaped as pairs (above); - the first-name pick (above); - a flag before a tab: `FLAG_IN_TEXT` takes `(?=[\s=])`; - PGP keys: `PRIVATE KEY(?: BLOCK)?-----`; - single-quoted and unquoted values. - **Listed in the README:** - `{option_name, option_value}`, a pair under other names; - an element value holding `>`. **Nit, the naming.** The group is `LOSES_ROWS` now: what loses rows, a collection or its key. The comment, the README and the CHANGELOG say `column-dropped` loses data too, but comes next because it is one flag a collection whatever the PR's padding. **Mutation:** 22 hand mutants of this round's code, 19 killed. - `VALUE` in upper case is equivalent under the `i` flag. - The backslash lookbehind was redundant and is removed. - Letting the DSN password cross `:` masks no less, and only costs time, which W28=B leaves to the README. **Tests:** 837 passed and 0 failed on Node 24 and on Node 22 (`node --test --test-force-exit`); 71 are in `test/data-diff.test.mjs`. One Node 22 run had round 3's 10 MB scan test over its 5 s bound under a load average near 50 (0.7 s alone), and passed when rerun. CI is green on `4ed6449`.
